A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiPRM research. All 15 pages of v2 and 17 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison; relocated tables and renumbered appendices can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original solution-selection and step-error-detection results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds boundary-perturbation and long-chain experiments, external baseline comparisons, and resource measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains prompt-based step reversal, parallel L2R/R2L scoring, dynamic MLP gating, minimum-score trajectory aggregation, the three training objectives, and Best-of-N inference. The new experiments test the existing method.

E1.justification: v3 adds a ProcessBench scenario with merged, split, and noisy step boundaries. The underlying training and evaluation datasets and mathematical tasks remain unchanged; the long-chain analysis selects a subset of existing evaluation data.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained L2R comparisons and internal controls, v3 Table 4 adds four external ProcessBench comparators: Math-Shepherd-PRM-7B, RLHFlow-PRM-Deepseek-8B, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Math-Shepherd, and Qwen2.5-Math-RM-72B. This substantially expands comparison against established models.

E3.justification: New protocols filter sequences above 1024 tokens for Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/BCE evaluation and introduce artificial ProcessBench boundary perturbations. Efficiency evaluation replaces theoretical FLOPs ratios with reported measured TFLOPS and adds peak memory. Original training settings, splits, and BON/F1 metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds two substantive robustness investigations: whether dynamic gating retains its advantage on long chains (Appendix D, Table 10), and whether bidirectional scoring tolerates ambiguous step boundaries (Section 4.4, Table 6). Existing component ablations, error profiles, qualitative cases, and aggregation sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose seed 1106 and different seeds for the two-model ensembles. Neither reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run variability; the new degradation percentages are result summaries, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and appendix values are retained. New results include external baseline scores, aggregate relative F1 drops of 5.24% versus 7.52% for BiPRM versus L2R under perturbation, and long-chain BON drops of 31.40% versus 37.56% for dynamic versus static fusion. Table 8/Appendix B add 10.034 versus 19.106 TFLOPS and 6.43 versus 6.65 GB peak memory for L2R versus BiPRM.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, directional-dependence arguments, gating equations, aggregation rule, and training losses in Equations 1–10 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty, generality, and efficiency claims. The headline 10.6% and 37.7% relative gains, 0.3% parameter overhead, and approximately 5% latency overhead are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations about long-chain gating stability, robustness to inconsistent segmentation, competitiveness with larger models, and modest memory overhead. The external-model advantage is subset-dependent: Table 4 beats the 72B comparator on GSM8K and Omni-MATH, but not MATH or OlympiadBench. Existing domain limitations and failure-case explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 replaces the promise of code release after acceptance with a GitHub repository address. Appendix A's software versions, hardware, and hyperparameters remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's availability or contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dong et al. (2024), Zhang et al. (2025), and three Gao et al. (2025) references. A short related-work addition connects bidirectional verification to multimodal and in-context-learning complexity; the existing positioning against BiRM remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds focused experimental passages, rewrites the efficiency appendix, and inserts a new Appendix D, shifting the former D/E to E/F. Affiliations, corresponding-author identification, and acknowledgments also change. Most existing prose and the main section order are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4, 6, and 10, changes the efficiency table's FLOPs column to TFLOPS, reorders Table 3 subsets, and resizes or relocates existing displays. Figure content and the overall two-column design are preserved; these are localized presentation changes.

improvement.justification: The external comparisons and targeted robustness tests address gaps in v2's empirical support, while memory measurements and a code address improve practical documentation. However, perturbation rates and long-subset sample counts are unspecified, and broad real-world robustness interpretations exceed the narrowly documented tests. These additions provide a useful but limited overall improvement.
